source_text:
ἐκκλησίᾳ· καὶ ἔσται ψόγος τῶν κρινομένων ὅτε δέονται καὶ τῶν ἐξουθενημένων
μᾶλλον ἢ τῶν σοφῶν· ὁ μὲν γὰρ τῷ λόγῳ ἀκολουθῶν, εἰ καὶ δεῖται κριτοῦ, δεῖται
μᾶλλον σοφοῦ, ἵνα νουθετηθῇ ἀπὸ τῆς σοφίας τοῦ σοφοῦ εἰσφέροντος αὐτῷ λόγους
οἰκοδομοῦντας. [vi 4–5] τοὺς ἐξουθενημένους οὖν ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τούτους καθίζετε·
πρὸς ἐντροπὴν ὑμῖν λέγω· οὕτως οὐκ ἔνι ἐν ὑμῖν οὐδεὶς σοφὸς ὃς δυνήσεται
ἀνακρῖναι ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ; Ἐγκαλεῖ τῇ Κορινθίων ἐκκλησίᾳ ὅτι
καίτοι ἐν μέσῃ τῇ Ἑλλάδι καθεζόμενοι σοφοὺς οὐκ εἶχον ἀληθινούς, καίτοι γε
προειπὼν ὅτι πολλοὶ ἐπαγγέλλονται σοφίαν παρ' αὐτοῖς· δι' οὓς καὶ εἶπεν τὸ Ὁ
δρα όμενο τοὺ οφοὺ ἐν τῇ πανουργίᾳ αὐτῶν. ἀλλ' οἱ μὲν εἰσὶ σοφοὶ τοῦ αἰῶνο
τούτου, οἱ δὲ σοφοὶ κατὰ θεόν. ᾔδει δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ἐκείνους· διὰ τοῦτο φησὶν Οὕτως
οὐκ ἔνι ἐν ὑμῖν σοφὸς ὃς δυνήσεται ἀνακρῖναι ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ; [vi 6]
ἀλλ' ἀδελφὸς μετὰ ἀδελφοῦ κρίνεται, καὶ τοῦτο ἐπὶ ἀπίστων; Ἔχομεν ἄρχοντας τῆς
ἐκκλησίας ἐφ' οὓς ὀφείλομεν ἀναφέρειν τὰς ἡμετέρας κρίσεις, ἵνα μὴ καταγελώμεθα
ἐν τοῖς τῶν ἐθνῶν δικαστηρίοις. [vi 7] ἤδη μὲν οὖν ἥττημα ὑμῖν ἐστιν ὅτι κρίματα
ἔχετε μεθ' ἑαυτῶν, οὐ μεμνημένοι τοῦ ∆ιὰ τί οὐχὶ μᾶλλον ἀποστερεῖσθε; ἀποστῶμεν
τῶν κριμάτων τῶν βημάτων τῶν ἐθνικῶν, τοῦ ἔχειν δίκας καὶ πράγματα. ὁ γὰρ
κρίματα ἔχων μετὰ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ ἤδη ἡττᾶται, καὶ ὁ ἀδικούμενος νενίκηκεν· ὁ
τυπτόμενος καὶ κακολογούμενος μηδὲ ἀμειβόμενος τὸν ταῦτα ποιοῦντα νενίκηκεν,
φυλάττει γὰρ τὴν ἐντολὴν τὴν λέγουσαν ∆ιὰ τί οὐχὶ μᾶλλον ἀδικεῖσθε; διὰ τί οὐχὶ
μᾶλλον ἀποστερεῖσθε; [vi 8] ἀλλ' ὑμεῖς ἀδικεῖτε καὶ ἀποστερεῖτε, καὶ τοῦτο
ἀδελφούς. Πᾶς μὲν οὖν ὁ ταῦτα ποιῶν ἁμαρτάνει· ὅσῳ δὲ τιμιώτερόν ἐστι τὸ ἀδικού
μενον πρόσωπον, τοσούτῳ τὸ ἁμάρτημα χαλεπώτερον. καὶ γὰρ εἰ ἀδικεῖ τις τὸν
μακάριον, δυνάμει Χριστὸν ἀδικεῖ καὶ Χριστὸν ἀποστερεῖ. [vi 9] ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι
ἄδικοι θεοῦ βασιλείαν οὐ κληρονομήσουσιν; Εἰ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ ἐστιν,
Χριστὸς δὲ ἡ δικαιο ύνη ἐστίν, ὁ δίκαιος βασιλείαν θεοῦ κληρονομεῖ ἐν Χριστῷ

pass_a_gloss: church; blame falls on litigants when they need even the despised rather than the wise. The one following the Word, if he needs a judge, needs a wise man so that he may be corrected by wisdom bringing upbuilding words. So seat the despised in the church. I speak for your shame. Is there truly among you no wise man able to examine between his brother? He accuses the Corinthian assembly that, though placed in the midst of Hellas, they lacked true wise men, though many among them advertised wisdom—on whose account he said he catches the wise in their cunning. Some are wise of this age; others wise toward God. Paul knew the former; therefore he asks whether there is among you a wise man able to examine between his brother. But brother is judged with brother, and this before unbelievers? We have church rulers to whom we should bring our cases, lest we be mocked in Gentile courts. Already it is a defeat for you that you have lawsuits among yourselves. Why not rather be deprived? Withdraw from Gentile platforms and from having suits and quarrels. The one who has suits with his brother is already defeated; the wronged one has won; the one struck and insulted who does not repay has won, keeping the command: Why not rather suffer wrong? Why not rather be deprived? But you do wrong and deprive, and that to brothers. Everyone doing this sins; and the more honored the injured person, the harsher the fault. If someone wrongs the blessed man, he in effect wrongs Christ and deprives Christ. Or do you not know the unjust will not inherit God’s kingdom? If God’s kingdom is in Christ and Christ is righteousness, the just inherits God’s kingdom in Christ who is righteousness; the one in the contrary state does not inherit. Do not be led astray: neither fornicators… Let no one lead you astray with plausible talk: God is merciful, kind, philanthropic; he remits sins. We must all be shown before Christ’s tribunal so each may receive what was done through the body, good or bad. Let no one plead: I was young; I was unmarried; before marriage I fornicated. Why did you not take a wife? Do you not trust that if someone ruins God’s temple, God will ruin him? Do you lift Christ’s members and make them a harlot’s members? The fornicator acts impiously toward the God of the whole. So do not be led astray: neither fornicators nor idolaters inherit God’s kingdom; nor adulterers. The fornicator ruins God’s temple; the adulterer also offends against the husband. Neither adulterers; nor the soft. We urge you too, boys, to keep your own time clean and not be stained with such feminine pollution. Nor will male-bed partners inherit God’s kingdom; may the church never find even one such. Then he descends to seeming lesser sins: nor thieves. Nearly all soldiers commit this theft-sin, not content with rations as the gospel taught, but shaking down and slandering. Liars in trade are thieves, not inheriting God’s kingdom; so also overreachers in trade are greedy; others drunkards; and he says revilers do not inherit God’s kingdom. Let sin reign over none; God’s kingdom must be clean of every fault and stumble so God may reign. All things are permitted me, yet not all benefit. All things are permitted me, yet I will not be ruled by anyone. One must stand above what one received power over—things which if done still are not sin. More ambitious lives live thus. Do we not have power to eat and drink? Do we not have power to lead about a sister-wife, as the remaining apostles and the Lord’s brothers and Cephas?
pass_b_english: church; and there will be blame on those judged when they need even the despised rather than the wise. For the one who follows the Word, if he needs a judge, needs rather a wise one, that he may be admonished by the wisdom of the wise man who brings him words that build up. Therefore seat those who are despised in the church. I say this to your shame. Is it so, that there is not among you anyone wise who will be able to decide between his brother? He charges the Corinthian church that, though seated in the middle of Greece, they had no true wise men, although he had said earlier that many among them profess wisdom—on whose account he also said: “He catches the wise in their craftiness” (1 Corinthians 3:19). But some are wise of this age, and others wise according to God. Paul knew those former ones; therefore he says: Is it so, that there is not among you a wise man who will be able to decide between his brother?

But brother goes to law with brother, and this before unbelievers? We have rulers of the church to whom we ought to bring our judgments, that we may not be laughed at in the courts of the nations. Already it is altogether a defeat for you that you have lawsuits with one another. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be defrauded? (1 Corinthians 6:7). Let us withdraw from the judgments of Gentile tribunals, from having lawsuits and disputes. For the one who has lawsuits with his brother is already defeated, and the one who is wronged has conquered; the one beaten and reviled who does not repay the one doing these things has conquered, for he keeps the command that says: Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be defrauded? But you wrong and defraud, and that your brothers. Everyone who does these things sins; and the more honorable the person wronged, the heavier the sin. For if someone wrongs the blessed one, he wrongs Christ in effect and defrauds Christ.

Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God? If the kingdom of God is in Christ, and Christ is righteousness, the righteous inherits the kingdom of God in Christ who is righteousness; and accordingly the one in the opposite state does not inherit the kingdom of God. Do not be deceived: neither the sexually immoral… Let no one deceive you with persuasive words: “God is merciful, kind, and loving toward humankind; he forgives sins.” We must all be manifested before the judgment seat of Christ, that each may receive the things done through the body, whether good or bad (2 Corinthians 5:10). Let no one make excuses: I was young; I was unmarried; before taking a wife I committed fornication. Why then did you not take a wife? Do you not believe that if anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy him? Do you take the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute? The one who fornicates acts impiously toward the God of all.

Do not be deceived, then: neither the sexually immoral nor idolaters will inherit the kingdom of God; and so neither adulterers. The one who fornicates destroys the temple of God; the adulterer, in addition, also sins against the husband. Neither adulterers, then; nor the soft / effeminate. We exhort you also, children, to keep your own season pure and not to be defiled with such womanish pollution. Nor will men who lie with men inherit the kingdom of God; and may it be far from the church that even one such be found. Then he descends also to sins that seem lesser, saying: nor thieves. This sin of theft nearly all who serve in the army commit, not content with their wages, as the gospel taught, but shaking people down and bringing false charges. And those who lie in business are thieves, not inheriting the kingdom of God; and so also those who overreach in business are greedy; and others are drunkards; and he says revilers also do not inherit the kingdom of God. Therefore let sin reign over no one; for the kingdom of God must be pure from all sins and stumblings, that God may reign.

All things are lawful for me, but not all things are helpful. All things are lawful for me, but I will not be mastered by anything (1 Corinthians 6:12). One must stand above the things over which one has received authority—things which, even if we do them, we will not sin. For those who live more ambitiously live in this way. Do we not have authority to eat and drink? Do we not have authority to take along a sister as wife, as also the other apostles and the brothers of the Lord and Cephas? (1 Corinthians 9:4–5).

choices.why: Paul’s forensic sense: already losing by suing a brother.
